ownership_reason: Only the gold looks at the characters of the short name: hops 1-3 apply the builder's settings to the Option the gold returns, hop 4 passes the name along and the facade only delegates and resets the builder. Once the gold has thrown for a name, no caller can recover the Option without creating it by other means, and no change to the name before the gold keeps the name '?'. The convention is pinned outside the gold: OptionValidator.validateOption, called by every Option constructor (among them the one the gold calls and the one Options.addOption(String, String, boolean, String) calls), accepts a one-character name that is a Java identifier part, '?' or '@' (its javadoc: 'a single character opt that is either ' '(special case), '?', '@' or a letter'; isValidOpt: isValidChar(c) || c == '?' || c == '@'), and requires every character of a longer name to be a Java identifier part; the facade's javadoc says 'if opt is not a valid character. See Option.'; testIllegalOptions and testBuilderIsResettedAlways pin the rest of the same rule on the same path and pass. The gold's javadoc promises an IllegalArgumentException only if there are non valid Option characters in opt, which '?' is not. The facade keeps the original finally around its one delegating call because the builder's settings and reset() are private to OptionBuilder; the reset runs whether or not the Option is created, as before. One-line edits above the gold that pass the trigger and the suite all replace the gold's result: creating the Option at a hop with the validating constructor instead of calling the next hop, answering '?' and '@' at a hop before the gold, or catching the gold's exception at a hop and creating the Option there.
